piece_title: W1-01 — the province streaming pump (Engine._streamProvince from _afterStep, plus release hysteresis)

bifurcation.note: This piece is judged on residency, frame cost and arrival behaviour, all of which are counters read off the running world. The two PNGs are illustration for the blog and for §8's falsification, not the basis of any score. RI-MTH01: no FPS claim is made anywhere; every millisecond figure is a per-fixed-step wall-clock measurement taken around loop.stepOnce()+_afterStep() with performance.now(), on SwiftShader, and is used only for comparison against another figure taken the same way in the same session.

environment_caveat.consequence: Absolute milliseconds in the fight, ride and displace runs (loadavg 12-17) are an UPPER BOUND. Rates (fraction of steps over 16.7 ms), counts, residency figures and within-run separations were taken at the same load in the same session and are load-robust. Both screenshots were taken at loadavg 22-26 and cost 47-53 s each.

reference_items.aggregation_note: RI-MTH07 aggregates min-over-axes across the item's OWN axes (does the piece name a consumer; does it demonstrate consumption by perturbation; is there a null control). C-tileM is not one of those axes — it is one of the five MODELS the piece ships, and RI-MTH07's rule fixes that MODEL at 0, not the item. All three of the item's axes are measured and pass, so the min is not 0; the orphan model is carried as the reason the item is 6 and not 9.

blind_comparisons.not_possible_reason: This piece is judged on counters read off the running world, not on appearance. RI-MTH01 forbids an FPS claim on SwiftShader and no such claim is made; the bifurcation axis is declared not-visual above.

checks.observed: In a 9,000-step fight in the province with the streamer live: 33 frames did streaming work and those 33 have mean 138.39 ms / p50 142.16 ms / max 448.95 ms, against p50 0.125 ms for the 8,967 frames that did none. 17 of 1,040 ROLL_IFRAME frames exceeded 16.7 ms and the worst frame in the run - 448.95 ms, did=5 (ground skin + ground cover disc) - landed INSIDE a roll's i-frame window. A 14-frame i-frame window is 233 ms; the frame is longer than the window it landed in. With MAX_CATCHUP=5 the fight freezes and resumes on one sampled input.
checks.why_this_is_ar1: ARBITRATION S1: inside the fight, Souls wins - and S1 as amended says Souls' authority is over how fighting works. A world-streaming subsystem that can stop a roll for a quarter of a second has taken a frame decision away from the fight. S26 forbids diluting AR-1 to cover ordinary defects, and this is not an ordinary defect: it is a Morrowind-side subsystem setting the schedule of a Souls-side frame.
checks.boundary_ruling: The builder assigns the ~59 ms rebuild to W1-01's updateSkin calibration. REJECTED as a handoff. updateSkin did not get more expensive in this change; it got CALLED DURING FIGHTS. Before this change request() ran on a teleport. The COST is W1-01's; the SCHEDULE is now _streamProvince's, and a subsystem that owns a schedule owns the frames it lands on.

checks.observed: The change adds no marker, no warp, no procedural loot and no soul-currency purchase. It streams ground. The one Souls-shaped affordance it touches - the death respawn - it only observes.

S17: nothing here slows the player down to buy streaming time. The crossing's own speed histogram puts 33,074 of 33,078 samples in the 1.99-2.01 m/s band, and _streamProvince runs after the step has already decided where the body went.

ar3.justification: The piece carries a boundary-crossing interaction in BOTH directions and both are measured here. The world's streaming schedule now reaches into the fight (a ground-skin rebuild landing inside ROLL_IFRAME), and the fight's own displacement reaches out into the world (the death respawn's 4,142.6 m jump driving the arrival burst). That is the opposite of sterile - and it is exactly why the seam has to be arbitrated rather than admired.

orphans.measured: request() computes tx0/tz0 from the module constant TILE_M (world/province.js:200) while stats() reports tileSizeM: this.tileM (:1145). Perturbing it desynchronises the reported geometry from the built geometry and nothing in the tree would notice.

consumption.note: The world-side consumer for the four that couple is Engine._afterStep() -> _streamProvince() -> Province.request()/pump(), observed as tiles that exist in province.tiles under a body that WALKED there - never as a harness return value.

status_reasons: RI-PLT03 is capped at 2 by two triggered hard fails (HF4, HF6), and that cap is what moves the mean, not a judgement that the streaming work is bad.
AR-1 fail: a 448.95 ms frame inside a roll's i-frame window, caused by a world-streaming refocus.
The single worst frame in the build is now the frame after a respawn: 483.96 ms, six consecutive frames totalling ~2,283 ms, and MAX_CATCHUP=5 turns that into ~2.2 s of DROPPED simulation time.
travelRide at 40 m/s puts 6.62% of steps over one 60 Hz frame and 5.53% over 50 ms, max 674.76 ms. Every budget constant in _streamProvince is sized for a 2.0 m/s walk.
The urgent branch's pump(2) sits ABOVE `if (discWork) return`, so 'one unit of streaming work per fixed step' is true for the trickle and false for the burst.
At viewpoints-province.json's declared settleFrames: 24 the ring is 10 of 25 with 15 still queued; full closure needs 384-512 frames.
province.tileM is an orphan knob introduced by this change.

AGAINST all of that: the defect the piece was sent to fix is CLOSED on every modality I could reach, verified with an independent instrument that was proved falsifiable, and the crossing is genuinely walked.

biggest_gap.what: The urgent tile-build branch in Engine._streamProvince() is exempt from the one-unit-of-work-per-step budget AND is evaluated BEFORE it, so any frame on which the body ARRIVES somewhere - a respawn, a teleport, a future fast-travel or cutscene relocation - pays a ~30-tile release plus updateSkin (15,625 vertices) plus updateCover plus updateNear plus two full _buildTile calls in one fixed step.
biggest_gap.why_it_matters: Measured on a real death in the province, the six frames after the respawn cost 337.01, 405.43, 483.96, 361.98, 222.64 and 472.46 ms - about 2,283 ms in total, against the builder's walking worst case of 133.8 ms. FixedLoop.MAX_CATCHUP is 5, so in mode 'play' the accumulator advances at most 83 ms of world and drops the remaining ~2.2 s into catchupDroppedMs. The world stops for two seconds at the exact moment a Souls player has just died and is looking for their bloodstain, which is the most latency-sensitive moment in the game outside a boss swing. The builder never saw it because every one of its runs was a walk, and a walk never enters this branch.

remedy.action: Make the urgent budget respect the work the frame has already done, and declare the arrival as a load boundary.
targets: game/src/engine.js _streamProvince(): move `if (discWork) return;` ABOVE the urgent branch, or change pump(STREAM_URGENT_TILES) to pump(discWork ? 1 : STREAM_URGENT_TILES). The tile under the body is queue[0] with d === 0 and one pump(1) places it; the other eight tiles of the 3x3 are 150-450 m away and can wait a frame each.
game/src/engine.js teleport() and the respawn path: wrap in _boundaryBegin('province_stream') / _boundaryEnd, per RI-PLT03 §B. A boundary you announce is not a hitch.

game/src/engine.js: skip the request() refocus while combat.player.state is inside ATK_* or ROLL_*, letting s.since keep counting. This is the AR-1 remedy and it is far cheaper than making updateSkin fast: a roll covers ~5 m against SKIN_REBUILD_M = 11, so nothing visible moves.

game/src/engine.js STREAM_REFOCUS_M and the disc rebuild distances: budget by METRES SINCE THE LAST REBUILD rather than by frames, so travelRide at 40 m/s gets the throughput it needs instead of a walk's.
remedy.acceptance: node tools/world/critic-prov-r1.mjs --mode displace reports worst_step_ms_after_jump <= 120 on a box at loadavg < 4, with frames_standing_on_no_ground still 0 and frames_until_near9_complete <= 16; --mode ride reports over_16_7 <= 1% of steps; --mode fight reports iframe_frames_over_16_7 = 0; --mode loop unchanged.

secondary_observations.what: The working tree does not boot. node tools/harness/boot-check.mjs exits 12 with 'this._installTopicSupply is not a function' (engine.js:320); a concurrent agent's in-flight edit to engine.js + character/converse.js with sim/quest/topic-supply.js untracked. Every measurement in this verdict was taken on a shadow tree pinned at HEAD=8734986. Any agent that uses smoke.mjs as a boot check will report green against a build no player could launch.

A posed capture camera demolishes the player's own world. With an override eye 2.4 km from the body and the 24-frame settle shoot.mjs actually uses, at the BODY: underfoot false, near-3x3 9 of 9 unbuilt, ring 0/25, tiles_resident 10. request() releases everything outside KEEP of the EYE. Clearing the pose recovers underfoot on frame 0 and the 3x3 by frame 4, but the ring takes 454 frames. NOT player-reachable - sim.camera.override is written only by Engine.camera() (engine.js:3823/3837/3873) and deathCamera() sets camera.deathFrame instead - but the capture daemon is a pooled warm browser, so any residency or settle read taken at the body between two posed requests sees a demolished province.

walkPath is broken independently of this piece. Fed a 1,200 m slice of the crossing spline it ran to maxFrames=400000, covered 59,873.7 m at a mean 8.98 m/s - 4.5x walking speed - and never arrived, offset_m 686.43, longest_stuck_frames 1. Residency was fine throughout so it does not affect this verdict, but every walkPath-based reachability number in the tree is worth re-reading.

travelRide is fare-gated at a cold start: boardTravel refuses every service with 'You have not walked the <leg> road. No one sells passage over ground you have not crossed.' That is good design and it bounds the exposure of the vehicle streaming defect - you can only ride a road you have already walked - but it also means the fastest movement modality in the build had never been driven by any probe before this one.

Release hysteresis causes CHURN, not a leak: 36-42 tile builds per 1.4 km lap of a closed circuit, i.e. the same tiles destroyed and rebuilt every time round, ~2.6 s of rebuild work per lap at the ~69 ms the builder attributes to a tile build. KEEP is currently set to the smallest value that stops the edge thrash and no larger.

Two small bookkeeping discrepancies in the builder's own report: the status file says the crossing took 35 samples where AFTER-crossing.json's summary.samples says 34; and the crossing artifact was itself taken at loadavg 12.54.

All 17 province viewpoints in tools/harness/viewpoints-province.json declare anchor: region_* states that do not exist in game/data/states. Flagged by the builder, not fixed, and not this change's; recorded here so it is not lost.

gap_closure.note: Independently verified with an instrument the builder did not write, on a movement path the builder did not test (raw stick + stepFrames(1)), and falsified by neutering the one call and watching every check invert.

corpus_extended.note: RI-PLT03's S4 and S5 are defined 'per minute of continuous WALKING'. This build's fastest movement is a 40 m/s vehicle, at which the same streamer produces 199 hitches per traversal minute against a walk's 9.3, and no check in the item would ever ask. The item needs a motion axis: every streaming budget should be evaluated at the fastest speed the build can actually move a body, not at the walk. Filed rather than worked around; the measurement is in corpus/90-verdicts/wave1/artifacts/W1-01-province-stream-r1/ride.json.

method_deviations.deviation: Two probes were written by this critic under orchestration/TOOL-LOOP.md rule 1 and are cited as evidence: tools/world/critic-prov-r1.mjs (modes modality, fight, displace, loop, posed, settle, raf, ride, plus a --break-fix falsification control) and tools/world/critic-prov-shot.mjs (photographs the same spot 750 m into a WALKED approach, with and without the pump).
method_deviations.why: The only province-streaming probe in the tree is tools/world/prov-stream.mjs, which is the builder's own and which measures a 2.0 m/s walk. Nothing in the tree drives travelRide, the rAF accumulator under real time, a fight with the streamer live, a death respawn, or a long closed loop, and nothing reads FixedLoop.stats.catchupClamps. Both probes read province.tiles/focus/discs only and never call request(), pump(), drain() or __HARNESS.streamAround(). Both were proved falsifiable before being trusted: --break-fix neuters Engine._streamProvince in the page and every residency check inverts (see artifacts modality-broken.json, settle-broken.json, displace-broken.json, raf-broken.json).

method_deviations.deviation: In --mode ride I set engine.travel.walked for every leg before calling boardTravel, and set gold to 100,000.
method_deviations.why: boardTravel refuses every service at a cold start ('You have not walked the stormhold-helstrom road'), so the vehicle modality is otherwise unreachable without first walking 23 simulated minutes of road. Granting the walked-road credit is the same class of concession as granting the fare: it opens the fare gate, it does not touch the streamer, and the thing under test - what _streamProvince does when the body moves at 40 m/s - is untouched by it. RI-MTH07's hand-feed prohibition is about feeding the PREDICATE under test, which this is not.

method_deviations.deviation: Every measurement was taken on a shadow tree produced by `git archive HEAD | tar -x` rather than on the working tree, with tools/node_modules symlinked.
method_deviations.why: The working tree does not boot (exit 12, this._installTopicSupply is not a function) because of a concurrent agent's in-flight edit. boot-check PASSES on the shadow tree before and after every measurement. The shadow tree is byte-identical to commit 8734986, which is stated in build.commit_sha, so every artifact is reproducible from that commit alone.

method_deviations.deviation: The builder's own null control (skinRadiusM 34 -> 17) is accepted from reports/world/province-stream/CONSUME-null-skin17.json rather than re-run.
method_deviations.why: It is a NEGATIVE control whose entire content is that it changed nothing in the arm under test, and the positive arm (radiusTiles 1/2/3 -> 9/25/49) was re-derived independently here from stats() rather than from the module constants. Re-running a null control that reports no change adds no discriminating power; re-deriving the positive arm does.

unmeasured.claim: quiet-box absolute milliseconds for the fight, ride and displace runs
unmeasured.reason: taken at loadavg 12-17 with several agents running. Rates, counts, residency figures and within-run separations were taken at the same load and are load-robust; the absolute worst-case figures are stated as upper bounds wherever they appear.

unmeasured.claim: whether the 448.95 ms i-frame frame is visible to a player as a MISSED INPUT
unmeasured.reason: that needs the input pipeline's own latency instrument driven through the rAF path, which does not exist in this tree.

unmeasured.claim: the province viewpoints' anchor: region_* states
unmeasured.reason: flagged by the builder as absent from game/data/states; not verified here and not this change's.

unmeasured.claim: streaming behaviour on the other travel modes (rootway 7 m/s, packet 6, barge 4, poler 2.8)
unmeasured.reason: only the fastest (rootspeak, 40 m/s) was driven. It is the worst case and the others interpolate between it and the walk, but that is arithmetic, not measurement.

self_audit.self_audit_note: ran_every_assigned_method is FALSE and the verdict is provisional on one point. RI-PLT03's Comparison method names tools/platform/load-run.mjs, hitch-census.mjs and stream-audit.mjs. load-run.mjs and hitch-census.mjs exist in the tree; stream-audit.mjs does not, and none of the three drives the province streamer. Under TOOL-LOOP rule 1 I built what the method specifies rather than skipping it — tools/world/critic-prov-r1.mjs computes S2, S4, S5, S6 and S9 directly, with a --break-fix falsification control — but it is a tool minted for this occasion and the reader must know that. The Tier-H half of RI-PLT03 (TTFP, device-class load times) refuses to emit without an attested real-GPU manifest and was correctly not attempted. Absolute milliseconds were taken at loadavg 12-17 and are upper bounds; the hard-fail triggers do not depend on them, because S5's threshold is 100 ms and the smallest arrival-burst frame I measured is 222.64 ms.
